newsitem.title: AFGHANISTAN: Taleban shell foes after fighting in northwest.
newsitem.headline: Taleban shell foes after fighting in northwest.

text.p: Taleban artillery gunners pounded positions of a northern alliance near Kabul on Wednesday morning after the Islamic militia reported heavy overnight fighting in the remote northwest.
A Taleban artillery commander was listening to reports from his spotter on the front line north of the capital before relaying new co-ordinates to his men.

"We are aiming at Masood's positions around Bagram airport," one of the gun crew told Reuters of ousted government military chief Ahmad Shah Masood. The airport lies 50 km (30 miles) north of the capital.

Every five minutes the Soviet-built 122 mm artillery piece roared, kicking up a cloud of dust. "You must open your mouth when it fires or you will hurt your ears," a young Taleban fighter told journalists helpfully.

The purist Islamic Taleban, who took Kabul in late September, are facing the forces Masood and Uzbek leader Abdul Rashid Dostum along a front line in a valley some 25-30 km (15-19 miles) north of Kabul.
The commander said the front had been quiet for the last two days apart from sporadic shelling by both sides.
Taleban jets took off and landed in Kabul airport on Wednesday morning, but it was not immediately clear how much damage, if any, they had inflicted.
"There has been no movement of ground forces since the enemy attacked the night before last. Last night was quiet and there has been no change in the positions," the commander said.
Reuters correspondent Chris Bird reported from Masood's side of the northern front that the two forces exchanged occasional artillery fire early on Wednesday but that it was mainly quiet.
However, the Taleban reported heavy overnight fighting against forces loyal to Dostum in the northwestern province of Badghis.

A Taleban spokesman contacted by telephone in the western city of Herat told the Pakistan-based Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) the Taleban had killed nine Dostum soldiers and captured 70 in overnight battles in the northern Ghormach district, about 20 km (13 miles) inside Badghis.
The spokesman said several hundred Taleban fighters had been sent recently to reinforce the fast-changing front line.
The Taleban captured Ghormach and Murghab in Badghis and the Qaysar district in the adjacent province of Faryab when they began an offensive against Dostum late last week.
The Taleban spokesman's report that fighting was now going on in Ghormach confirmed reports from Kabul on Tuesday that Dostum's forces had driven the Islamic militants back.

Kabul-based sources said on Tuesday that 2,000 men sent by Dostum under General Malik (one name) to meet the threat on a new front had counter-attacked on Sunday, seizing the town of Murghab, some 60 km (40 miles) inside Badghis province.
If Dostum could recapture Badghis, he would be in a position to threaten the western city of Herat where there is a big population of ethnic Tajiks, cousins to the people of Masood.

The Taleban say an attack by the alliance forces north of Kabul on Monday night was repulsed with heavy casulaties. They say that 150 alliance fighters were killed and 400 wounded. There has been no independent confirmation of the casualty toll.
In a news conference on Tuesday the Taleban information minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told journalists that the Taleban were waging jihad -- holy war -- against the alliance.
"The Ulema (Islamic Scholars) has given a verdict that jihad against Dostum and his allies is legal," he said.
"Jihad is declared against all who undermine Moslem institutions. Dostum has stood against Moslem authority and therefore we have declared jihad against him," Mutaqi said through an interpreter.
The northern alliance, formally known as the Supreme Defence Council of Afghanistan, has vowed to push the Taleban out of Kabul and take the rest of the country from them.
